interpretation_notes: CPU is the whole WeChat process, not plugin-only CPU; one fully occupied core is 100%.
CPU peak is a roughly one-second sample peak, not an instantaneous spike.
Frame counts are classified frame-lifetime records. The ratio is hitch records divided by known frame-lifetime records, not an inferred number of dropped display refreshes.
Legacy Core Animation FPS estimates are device scope and are not interchanged with frame-lifetime event density or used to compute dropped frames.

Idle and switch-system captures required manual host postprocessing stop signals after their recording time limits and saved with exit 0. Target CPU windows cover 100%; original capture-result files are preserved.
Action windows were manually selected after operator start cues. Exact stop-cue timestamps were not recorded; analysis boundaries are conservative choices, not instrumented per-action markers.
Idle and switch-system frames are exported at ALL device/display scope. Only messages and scroll have independently verified SINGLE target scope.

Idle, messages and scroll exported Nominal thermal state. Switch-system changed from Nominal to Fair at t=40.357947541 s; its main window contains 15.357947541 s Nominal and 29.642052459 s Fair. These are not thermally controlled comparisons; Fair alone does not establish throttling or cause.
